q: An ammeter is a device used for measuring _____.
e: An ammeter is specifically designed to measure electric current.

q: A voltmeter is a device used for measuring _____.
e: A voltmeter is specifically designed to measure potential difference (voltage).

q: Ammeters and voltmeters are constructed based on the principle of a _____.
e: Both ammeters and voltmeters are modifications of a moving coil galvanometer.

q: A moving coil galvanometer is a sensitive electromagnetic device which can measure low currents even of the order of a few _____.
e: The moving coil galvanometer can measure low currents of the order of a few microamperes.

q: In a moving coil galvanometer, the coil is suspended in a uniform _____ magnetic field.
e: The coil is suspended in a uniform radial magnetic field.

q: A cylindrical soft iron core is positioned inside the galvanometer coil to improve the strength of the magnetic field and to make the field _____.
e: The soft iron core improves the magnetic field strength and makes the field radial.

q: The spring in a moving coil galvanometer is used to produce a _____ which balances the magnetic torque.
e: The spring produces a counter torque to balance the magnetic torque, allowing a steady angular deflection.

q: The principle of function of a moving coil galvanometer is that the current-carrying coil when placed in an external magnetic field experiences _____.
e: The coil experiences a magnetic torque when current flows through it in an external magnetic field.

q: The angle through which the galvanometer coil is deflected is proportional to the _____ of current in the coil.
e: The deflection angle is directly proportional to the magnitude of the current in the coil.

q: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting it in parallel with a wire of low resistance called _____ resistance.
e: A low resistance wire connected in parallel to convert a galvanometer to an ammeter is called a shunt resistance.

q: The formula for calculating the shunt resistance $r$ is _____.
e: Since the voltages are equal in parallel, $i R_G = (I - i) r$, which rearranges to $r = \frac{i}{I - i} R_G$.

q: An ammeter is a _____ resistance device.
e: An ammeter must have very low resistance so it does not significantly alter the current it is measuring.

q: An ammeter is connected in _____ with the circuit component.
e: To measure the current flowing through a component, the ammeter must be connected in series with it.

q: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting it in series with a _____ resistance resistor.
e: A high resistance resistor (multiplier) is connected in series to convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter.

q: The formula for calculating the multiplier resistance $R$ for a voltmeter is _____.
e: From $V = i(R_G + R)$, solving for $R$ gives $R = \frac{V}{i} - R_G$.

q: A voltmeter is a _____ resistance device.
e: A voltmeter must have high resistance so it draws minimal current and does not alter the potential difference it is measuring.

q: A voltmeter is connected in _____ with the circuit component.
e: To measure the potential difference across a component, the voltmeter must be connected in parallel with it.

q: The moving coil galvanometer coil is made up of many turns of fine _____ wire.
e: The textbook specifies that the coil is made of many turns of fine copper wire.

q: It is necessary for the shunt of an ammeter to have a very low resistance so that it can _____.
a: measure large currents without affecting the circuit
e: A very low shunt resistance ensures most of the current bypasses the delicate galvanometer coil, allowing measurement of large currents with minimal circuit disruption.

q: To convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter reading up to a higher voltage, the value of the multiplier resistance must be _____.
e: According to $R = \frac{V}{i} - R_G$, a higher maximum voltage $V$ requires a larger multiplier resistance $R$.
